edits.old: 1. Understand the target. In "meaning", briefly state the supplied subject's meaning and level of generality, including its required details and relationships. Do not narrow or broaden it to fit the post.
edits.new: 1. Understand the supplied subject. In "meaning", briefly state the supplied subject's meaning and level of generality, including its required details and relationships. Do not narrow or broaden it to fit the post.

edits.old: 2. Determine whether it is expressible. Before constructing the mask, decide whether the source wording can express the target at exactly its level of generality: all required meaning, details and relationships must be expressible, without having to include meaning the target does not specify. The wording may be spread across sentences. Set "expressible" to true only if both conditions can be met; otherwise set it to false. In "evidence", briefly identify the available wording or explain which required meaning is unavailable or which extra meaning is unavoidable.

edits.old: 3. Construct the mask. If "expressible" is true, choose fragments for the meaning they contribute to the target in the full note. Use the relationships already established in the note to connect those meanings; do not select additional wording just to make a connection explicit if it adds meaning the target does not require. Keep the target's required details and relationships and exclude added meaning and specificity. Include all contributions to the target, including repetitions; sharing a word or concept with the target is not sufficient. Individual fragments need not express the whole subject; the complete mask must. Include meaningful parts of words and hashtags by the same standard. Fragments need not form grammatical prose. If "expressible" is false, return an empty "mask" array.
